title: Hierarchical segment demotion + request-thermostat and soft-fallback for OOM avoidance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent OOMs under mixed latency/throughput workloads when continuous batching and KV cache buildup collide (long-tail prefixes + a few huge requests). Current eviction strategies are global and reactive; they cause abrupt failures or expensive synchronous spills that break SLOs.

Goal: Implement a graded memory-pressure mitigation strategy that prevents hard OOMs by combining (1) hierarchical KV segment demotion (hot->warm->cold), (2) a per-worker request-thermostat that throttles/defers low-priority admission, and (3) a nonblocking soft-fallback path that reroutes requests to compact model variants or token-trimmed execution when headroom is insufficient. Focus on graceful degradation, fast retries, and predictable SLO behavior.

Design summary: 
- Hierarchical segment demotion: partition KV cache by "segment affinity" (recent prefixes, session-affinity, large-context sessions). On memory pressure, demote segments progressively: first convert warm segments to a quantized snapshot format (4-bit compact), then evict cold segments to disk-backed cache asynchronously. Demotion is prioritized by recent hit rate and request-criticality.
- Request-thermostat: each worker maintains a moving headroom estimate and a token-bank for admission. Requests are scored by priority (interactive vs batch, customer SLA) and estimated peak transient memory. Low-priority requests can be delayed up to a configurable window; high-priority requests may trigger accelerated demotion or fallback.
- Soft-fallback: if admission still fails, the runtime attempts quick fallbacks in order: (a) run on compact quantized model variant (model-mini), (b) run with prefix trimming (preserve last N tokens), (c) fall back to stateless reranker/approximate response generator. Fallbacks are tagged in tracing, and the system instruments output-quality regression metrics.

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Demotion adds CPU overhead for quantization and async writes; must be bounded to avoid impacting latency. Use background worker pools with rate limits.
- Prefetch budgets and demotion heuristics require tuned thresholds per-instance class. Start with conservative defaults and expose knobs in Dedicated/Private.
- Some customers will prefer deterministic behavior over soft-fallback; provide an opt-out policy and SLA-tier binding.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) No hard OOMs in our simulated mixed workload benchmark (1M requests with 5% pathological long prefixes) for 72 hours on standard test fleet.
2) Median latency degradation under pressure < 1.4x and p95 degradation < 2.0x compared to baseline.
3) Successful demotion + async spill end-to-end path with < 5% CPU budget overhead on worker under median load.
4) Fallback path returns syntactically valid responses and is traced; automated eval shows < 2.5% quality regression for fallback-eligible requests.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spike): small prototype of hierarchical segment bookkeeping and demotion cost model; microbench quantization snapshot time and size.
- Phase 2: implement request-thermostat admission logic, integrate with continuous batching admission hook.
- Phase 3: implement soft-fallback runner and annotate traces/metrics.
- Phase 4: end-to-end integration test and long-run soak with chaos (induce memory spikes, slow disks).

Rollout plan: Canary on runtime-1.21 in a Dedicated pool (low SLO tier) for 2 weeks, then widen to more fleets. Provide console flags to visualize demotion events and fallback counts.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Spike complete: prototype for segment demotion bookkeeping implemented. Hot/warm/cold classification uses LRU windows + request tagging. Observed quantize snapshot (fp16->4-bit) reduces KV footprint by ~3.6x in synthetic workload.

2026-02-25 - Design review with reliability: agreed to decouple demotion scheduler from admission path to avoid latency regressions; use token-bucket for background CPU budget. Action: add throttling to async demotion worker.

2026-02-27 - Engineering note: request-thermostat integrates into batch-admission hook. We need estimate model for peak transient memory per request; Connor to instrument recent production traces to build estimator (ENG-13442).

2026-03-01 - Bench results (preliminary): 72h mixed-sim run eliminated hard OOMs but p95 latency rose by 1.6x in the worst case. Need to tune demotion aggressiveness and fallback thresholds. Added 'aggressive demotion' flag for canary toggles.
2026-03-04 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1678 - implements demotion bookkeeping + quantize snapshot worker. Needs tests and telemetry hooks.

2026-03-05 - Review feedback from ML infra: ensure fallbacks are evaluated against quality regression tests before returning; add callback to evaluation harness to avoid silent quality drops. Will wire into Optimize eval pipeline.
